description: Up to 50 parcels in any loaded state in one call (a loan tape, a broker's list, a client's accounts), each item naming one parcel by exactly one of: urn (a FactLot parcel URN); apn with state_fips and county_fips (3 digits), or with a 5-digit county_fips alone (as registry_resolve_parcel takes them); or address with the optional place fields registry_search_address takes (state, city, postal_code, county_fips). ref, your own row id, is echoed back. Each item is answered as the single tools answer it: registry_get for a URN, registry_resolve_parcel for an account, registry_search_address (20 results) for an address, then registry_get on the URN found. results lists one entry per item in input order (index, ref, by: urn, account or address, status): found gives parcel, a compact row: urn, label, record_status, account, property_category, use_code, improvement_area_sf, year_built, value (the newest roll year's entry of registry_get's value_history: tax_year, market and appraised value, as_of, value types, file and each value's citation), owner_of_record (the owner of record fact exactly as registry_get gives it, with the entity linked to it, or null; organisations only, natural persons are never stored), citations (each field's fact id, document id, locator and as-of date), sources (each cited document with its title, URI, read date, licence, ai_use and redistribution: relay them) and warnings; an address item also gives match (exact, and how many parcels the search returned). not_found gives message and coverage exactly as the single tool's miss gives them (the reason: county or state not loaded, street or house number not held); a URN not in the registry also carries registry_get's NotFound as error, with the same coverage registry_resolve_parcel gives for that county. An address is found when exactly one search result is exact, or when the search returned one parcel and it is in the place the address names; exact means the same street address and unit (the label's street line, normalized as the address index normalizes it, 'Street' = 'St', is the query's, a unit written as a bare number after the street counting as the unit, and both name the same unit or neither does) in the place the address names (when it names a city or ZIP code, in its text or the city and postal_code fields, the label has that ZIP code or city). Otherwise it is ambiguous, with reason: several_places (the address names no city or ZIP code and the results are in more than one county; a parcel is never picked across counties), same_address (several parcels have the address exactly: separate accounts at one address), place_differs (the one parcel found is not shown in the place named) or no_exact_match; candidates lists up to 5 of the search's result cards (the exact ones first; never an owner), with matches and a message. error gives the item's own error, so it does not fail the others: a wrong combination of fields (two of urn, apn and address, a field another mode takes, a missing county), a malformed or non-parcel URN, or an item the registry could not answer (RegistryUnavailable; after 5 such items the rest are not sent and say not attempted, and when no item at all is answered the whole call fails with RegistryUnavailable). An item whose fields fail the input schema (a wrong type, an unknown field, an empty ref, a URN over 500 characters) fails the whole call with InputError, uncharged. summary counts items, found, not_found, ambiguous and errors. On the hosted API this batch tool needs a Pro or Team key, and each item counts as the one call that identifies its parcel would count on its own (registry_resolve_parcel for an account or a URN, registry_search_address for an address): a found or ambiguous item counts one registry lookup; an item that finds nothing inside loaded coverage, a URN not in the registry included, is an answer that finds nothing (not counted up to an hourly limit, counted past it); a miss outside loaded coverage and an item with an error count none; the call needs one lookup per item left in the allowance to run, and one MCP request may make at most 500 registry service calls (an item counts 2), so a batch call past that is refused whole, uncharged. Facts as the sources publish them: not an appraisal, a valuation opinion or advice. Requires a FactLot Registry (public-record facts about commercial property, each cited to the source file and record).

items.description: The parcels (1–50), each by exactly one of urn, apn (with its county) or address.

address.description: Street address, e.g. '1200 Main St, Houston, TX 77002', searched as registry_search_address searches it.

apn.description: Parcel or account number as the county prints it (see registry_resolve_parcel), with state_fips and county_fips.

city.description: With address: city; orders the matches, never filters.

county_fips.description: With apn: 3-digit county FIPS with state_fips, or 5 digits alone ("48201"). With address: keeps the search to that county (5 digits, or 3 with state).

postal_code.description: With address: ZIP code; orders the matches, never filters.

ref.description: Your own id for this row (a loan number, a client account), echoed back with its answer.

state.description: With address: state, two letters or full name; keeps the search to that state.

name: registry_lookup_batch
title: Look up many parcels (batch)
